 Judgment
1. The claimant is the appellant in this appeal.
An extent of 37.51 Ares belonging to the claimant was acquired as per Section 4(1) Notification dated 5.12.2007, under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, for "Tsunami Rehabilitation Project".
The Land Acquisition Officer awarded compensation fixing land value at the rate of Rs.31,273/- per Are.

The Reference Court fixed the land value at Rs.57,000/- per Are relying on Ext.A2 judgment of this Court in LAA No.579 of 2011 in which the land acquired as per the very same Notification is involved.

The land of the appellant is categorized under 1(c), i.e.,
the property having access to a pathway.
The property involved in Ext.A2 is category 1(b), i.e., the property having access through Panchayat Road.
In Ext.A2, this Court fixed the land value at Rs.60,000/- per Are for category 1(b) property.
The Reference 2025:KER:39608 LA.APP. NO. 65 OF 2016 Court fixed the land value at Rs.57,000/-, reducing the land value fixed in Ext.A2 by 5%.
This appeal is filed for the enhancement of the compensation awarded by the Reference Court.
2. I heard the learned counsel for the appellant, Sri. C. Rajendran and the learned Senior Government Pleader, Smt. Rekha C. Nair, who appeared for the respondents.

3. The contention of the learned counsel for the appellant is that it is proved from Ext. C1 Commission report and C1(a) Plan that the property is situated on the side of a Panchayat Road and not a pathway.
In Ext.C1 report, it is specifically stated that the acquired property is situated on the side of a tar road having regular traffic.
Hence, the Reference Court ought to have included the property in Category No.1(b) and awarded the same value fixed by this Court in Ext.A2 judgment.
On the other hand, the learned Senior Government Pleader contended that the acquisition was of the year 2007, whereas the Commission was taken only in the year 2014.
The Reference Court has rejected the contention based on Ext.C1(a) on the specific ground that there are chances of developments in the area after the acquisition of the property.

sentences.text: I have considered the rival contentions.
6. In Ext.A2, this Court has fixed land value with respect to category 1(b) property.
The respondents have included the property belonging to the appellant in category No.1(c).
Ext.X1 is the Mahazar prepared by the officers.
It would show that only a pathway was there on the side of the road at the time of acquisition.
The acquisition was in the year 2007, whereas the commission was taken only in the year 2014.
The Reference Court has specifically referred to the reasons for refusing to rely on the Commission Report.
The Reference Court specifically 2025:KER:39608 LA.APP. NO. 65 OF 2016 referred to the evidence of AW2 that even families started residing in the acquired land.
When a land is acquired for public purpose, it is quite usual that there would be development in the area after the acquisition.
There is no evidence before the Court that a Panchayat Road access to the acquired property was there as on the date of acquisition.
Considering the fact that the commission was taken in the year 2014, it could not be relied on to find Panchayath road access as the same was taken after seven years of the acquisition.
7. Hence, I do not find any ground or reason to interfere with the impugned judgment.

Accordingly,
the L.A. Appeal is dismissed.
